testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What color is the ABS malfunction lamp?
questions.explanation: ABS malfunction lamps are yellow.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park your vehicle.

questions.question: What must truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: How is friction created inside a brake drum?

options.text: The brake shoes push against each other.
The brake shoes separate from the axle.
The brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction inside a brake drum is created when the brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle with air brakes should leak no more than 5 psi in one minute during a static leakage test. If it leaks faster, something needs repair and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: What equipment do truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Other vehicles with air brakes built after March 1, 1998 also require ABS.

questions.question: Where are braking mechanisms located?
questions.explanation: Braking mechanisms are located inside a brake drum. Drum brakes are attached to the wheels on the axles of a vehicle.

questions.question: What happens when you press and release the brake pedal unnecessarily?

options.text: Air releases faster than the compressor can replace it.
More air is added to the brake system.
The brake pedal becomes harder to press.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air releases faster than the compressor can replace it.
questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal unnecessarily lets air out faster than the compressor can replace it. This may lower air pressure too much and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: What does the service brake system do?

options.text: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving.
Applies and releases the parking brakes.
Applies and releases the emergency brake.
Applies and releases the axle brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving.
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three systems: service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake. The service brake system applies and releases brakes when you use the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Lift the brake pedal toward them.

questions.explanation: To stop normally in an air-braked vehicle, press down the brake pedal and control the pressure for a smooth, safe stop.

questions.question: The ____ between an air compressor and reservoir tank stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is installed between the air compressor and the first main reservoir. It stops air from escaping the system if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: How often should you drain air tanks with manual drains?
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks with manual drains at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: Air tank drains are used to:

options.text: Allow rain water to enter air tanks.
Remove water and oil from air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains that remove water and compressor oil. If these materials build up, they can damage the air brake system.

questions.question: All air tanks must have:
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks must have drain valves. These valves remove accumulated oil and water and can be manual or automatic.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. Built-up water and oil can damage the brakes.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes:
questions.explanation: To stop normally in a vehicle with air brakes, press down the brake pedal.

questions.question: The air compressor is connected to the:
questions.explanation: The air compressor is connected to the engine by gears or a belt. It can be cooled by air or by the engine cooling system.

questions.question: If an air compressor has a belt drive, the belt should be checked to make sure it is:
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor drive belt before each drive. Check that it is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: For a double combination vehicle, the maximum air leakage rate during an applied leakage test is ____ per minute.
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle should have a maximum air loss rate of 4 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate allowed for a triple combination vehicle during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: You need to know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A triple combination vehicle should not lose more than 6 psi of air per minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, what minimum air pressure must build in both systems?
questions.explanation: Wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how many seconds should it take for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi?
questions.explanation: When inspecting a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems in about 45 seconds.

questions.question: What happens if one air brake system has low pressure in a vehicle with dual air brakes?

options.text: The other system will send air to help the low-pressure system.
The front or rear brakes may not work properly.
The low system will use a backup system to refill the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front or rear brakes may not work properly.
questions.explanation: If one air system has very low pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. Stop the vehicle safely and have the air system fixed.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: Controls when the compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
Controls how fast air leaves the storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air entering the storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air leaving the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Controls when the compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
